examples.ko: 중요한 서류는 잘 간수해 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to keep important documents safe.

examples.ko: 여권은 잃어버리지 않게 가방 깊숙이 간수했어요.
examples.en: I stored my passport deep in my bag so I wouldn't lose it.

examples.ko: 귀한 물건이라서 아이 손이 닿지 않게 간수해요.
examples.en: It's a precious item, so I keep it out of the children's reach.

examples.ko: 통장을 어디에 간수했는지 기억이 안 나요.
examples.en: I can't remember where I put my bankbook for safekeeping.
Grandmother kept her money in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 비싼 카메라니까 여행 중에도 잘 간수하세요.
examples.en: It's an expensive camera, so keep it safe during the trip too.

explain: '보관하다'와 비슷하지만, 잃어버리거나 상하지 않게 조심해서 잘 둔다는 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 '잘 챙기다', '보관하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '간수하다'는 어른들이 하는 말처럼 들릴 때가 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to '보관하다' (to store), but it stresses putting something carefully so it won't be lost or damaged. In daily speech '잘 챙기다' or '보관하다' are more common, and '간수하다' can sound like something an older person would say.

en: be furnished with; be equipped with; be provided

examples.ko: 이 방에는 기본 가구가 모두 구비되어 있어요.
examples.en: This room is provided with all the basic furniture.
To apply, the documents have to be prepared first.
The hotel has been well equipped with the necessary facilities.

examples.ko: 응급 약품이 구비되어 있는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether emergency medicine is stocked.

examples.ko: 구비되는 장비가 많아서 따로 가져올 게 없어요.
examples.en: So much equipment is provided that there is nothing to bring.

examples.ko: 도서관에 새 컴퓨터가 구비되고 나서 이용자가 늘었어요.
examples.en: After new computers were installed in the library, more people started using it.

explain: 구비되다는 필요한 것이 이미 갖춰져 있을 때 써요. 숙소 안내나 공고문에서 '구비되어 있다' 모양이 가장 많아요. 말할 때는 '있어요', '갖춰져 있어요'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: This is used when what is needed is already in place. In lodging notices and announcements, the pattern '구비되어 있다' (is provided) is the most common. In speech, '있어요' or '갖춰져 있어요' is more relaxed.

examples.en: The heating and cooling in this building work very well.

examples.ko: 사무실 냉난방 비용이 너무 많이 나와요.
examples.en: The office heating and cooling costs are too high.
I bought an air conditioner that can both cool and heat.

examples.ko: 도서관은 냉난방이 완비돼 있어서 공부하기 좋아요.
examples.en: The library is fully equipped with heating and cooling, so it's good for studying.

examples.ko: 냉난방을 줄이면 전기 요금을 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you cut back on heating and cooling, you can save on electricity.

examples.ko: 이 집은 월세에 냉난방비가 포함돼 있어요.
examples.en: In this house, the monthly rent includes heating and cooling costs.

explain: 여름의 냉방과 겨울의 난방을 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요. 부동산 광고나 건물 안내에서 '냉난방 시설'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It covers summer cooling and winter heating in a single word. You often see it in real estate ads and building information, as in '냉난방 시설'.

examples.ko: 벽에 도료를 바르기 전에 먼저 닦아요.
examples.en: I wipe the wall first before applying paint.

examples.ko: 이 도료는 물에 강해서 욕실에 좋아요.
examples.en: This coating resists water, so it's good for bathrooms.
The paint smell was strong, so I opened the window.

examples.ko: 배에 칠하는 도료는 일반 페인트와 달라요.
examples.en: The coating applied to ships differs from regular paint.
I applied a new coat of paint to the old iron gate.
They say it takes a day for the paint to dry.

explain: 페인트, 니스, 래커처럼 표면에 칠하는 재료를 두루 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 '페인트'를 많이 쓰고, '도료'는 공사 설명이나 제품 설명, 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It broadly covers materials applied to a surface, like paint, varnish and lacquer. In daily talk '페인트' is commonly used, while '도료' often appears in construction explanations, product descriptions and news.

examples.en: We put a fence all around the field.
They have put up a tarp all around the construction site.

examples.ko: 마당에 담을 둘러치면 집이 더 안전해 보여요.
examples.en: If you put a wall around the yard, the house looks safer.

examples.ko: 텐트 주변에 줄을 둘러쳐서 들어오지 못하게 했어요.
examples.en: We strung a rope around the tent so no one could come in.
We received guests in a room surrounded by a folding screen.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 임시로 막을 둘러치는 중이에요.
examples.en: We are setting up a temporary screen around the front of the house.

explain: 울타리, 담, 병풍처럼 세우거나 걸어서 빙 둘러 막을 때 써요. '두르다'는 목도리처럼 몸에 감을 때도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요. 말로 하는 변명은 '둘러대다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you set up or hang something like a fence, wall or screen to enclose an area. '두르다' is broader and also covers things like wrapping a scarf around the body. For making an excuse in words, the verb is '둘러대다'.

examples.ko: 마대에 쌀을 가득 담아 창고에 쌓았어요.
examples.en: I filled the sacks with rice and piled them up in the warehouse.
At the construction site, we gathered the trash in sacks and threw it out.

examples.ko: 마대 자루가 무거워서 혼자 못 들겠어요.
examples.en: The sack is heavy, so I can't lift it by myself.
We put the potatoes in sacks and loaded them on the truck.

examples.ko: 청소할 때 마대 걸레로 바닥을 닦았어요.
examples.en: When cleaning, I wiped the floor with a mop.
The sack is worn out and has holes.

explain: 거친 천으로 만든 큰 자루예요. 곡식, 감자, 쓰레기를 담을 때 쓰고, '마대 걸레'처럼 대걸레 이름에도 들어가요. 자루나 포대와 비슷하게 쓰지만 마대는 거친 천이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a large sack made of coarse cloth, used for grain, potatoes and trash. The word also appears in '마대 걸레', a type of mop. It is used like '자루' or '포대', but 마대 carries the feel of rough fabric.

examples.ko: 밀폐된 공간에서는 환기를 자주 해야 해요.
examples.en: In an enclosed space, you need to ventilate often.

examples.ko: 이 병은 뚜껑을 꽉 닫으면 완전히 밀폐돼요.
examples.en: This bottle becomes fully sealed when you close the lid tightly.
The room was sealed off, so it felt stuffy.
If the food isn't sealed, it spoils quickly.

examples.ko: 밀폐되는 구조라서 소리가 밖으로 안 나가요.
examples.en: It has a sealing structure, so sound doesn't go outside.

examples.ko: 창문이 밀폐돼 있어서 바깥 소음이 거의 안 들려요.
examples.en: The windows are sealed, so you can hardly hear noise from outside.

explain: '닫히다'는 문이나 뚜껑이 닫힌다는 뜻만 담지만, '밀폐되다'는 안팎이 완전히 막혀 공기가 안 통하는 상태를 말해요. '밀폐된 공간', '밀폐된 용기'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '막히다'는 길이나 구멍이 막힌다는 말이라 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: '닫히다' only says a door or lid is closed, but '밀폐되다' describes a state completely blocked off so no air passes. It is often used as '밀폐된 공간' or '밀폐된 용기'. '막히다' is for roads or holes being blocked, so its use is different.

examples.ko: 차 번호판이 흙에 덮여서 안 보였어요.
examples.en: The car's license plate was covered in mud and couldn't be seen.
The entrance of the parking lot reads license plates automatically.
A blue license plate means an electric car.
I lost my motorcycle's plate and had a new one made.
I took a photo of the license plate and reported it.
It's a new car, so the plate is still shiny.

explain: 대부분 자동차 번호판을 떠올려요. 은행이나 병원에서 뽑는 번호는 '번호표'라고 해서 달라요. '번호판을 달다/떼다/가리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Most people picture a car's license plate. The number you draw at a bank or hospital is a 번호표, which is different. It goes with 번호판을 달다, 떼다, and 가리다.

examples.en: I put a poster up on the wall.
Please post the notice on the door.
Some schools have you attach a name tag to your bag.
I stuck a label on the box and then sent it.
The spot you attach it to must be clean for it to last.
Attach the receipt to the form and then submit it.

explain: '붙이다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '부착하다'는 안내문, 스티커, 장치처럼 격식 있는 글이나 설명서에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 '붙이다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '붙이다' but appears in formal writing such as notices, stickers, devices, and manuals. In everyday talk people almost always say '붙이다'.

en: separate recyclables; sort trash for recycling

examples.en: Every Sunday evening I sort the trash for recycling.
Plastic must be sorted separately.
In apartments, we sort recycling on a set day.
I learned how to sort recycling together with the kids.
I put the sorted bottles out at the recycling area.
It is better to wash things clean before sorting them for recycling.

explain: 종이, 플라스틱, 유리, 캔처럼 재활용할 쓰레기를 종류별로 나누어 버리는 것이에요. 한국에서는 아파트마다 '분리수거 하는 날'이 따로 있어요. 음식물 쓰레기는 따로 버리는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means separating recyclable trash such as paper, plastic, glass and cans by type. In Korea each apartment complex has its own 분리수거 day. Food waste is usually thrown away separately.

examples.en: I put an emergency flashlight in the drawer.

examples.ko: 이 약은 비상용이니까 함부로 먹지 마세요.
examples.en: This medicine is for emergencies, so don't take it carelessly.

examples.ko: 차 트렁크에 비상용 타이어가 실려 있어요.
examples.en: There is a spare emergency tire in the car trunk.
I carry a little cash for emergencies.

examples.ko: 집마다 비상용 물과 식량을 준비해 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good for every home to keep emergency water and food ready.

examples.ko: 지진에 대비해서 비상용 가방을 싸 뒀어요.
examples.en: I packed an emergency bag in case of an earthquake.

explain: '비상용 + 명사' 또는 '비상용으로', '비상용이다'처럼 써요. '예비용'은 미리 하나 더 준비해 둔 것이고, '비상용'은 위급할 때 쓰려고 준비한 것이라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used as '비상용 + noun', '비상용으로' or '비상용이다'. '예비용' means an extra one prepared in advance, while '비상용' is something kept for use in an urgent situation.

en: be provided; be kept on hand

examples.ko: 호텔 방에는 수건과 비누가 비치되어 있어요.
examples.en: Towels and soap are provided in the hotel room.
Fire extinguishers are being placed along every hallway of the building.

examples.ko: 병원 대기실에 잡지가 비치된 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many hospital waiting rooms have magazines on hand.

examples.ko: 도서관에는 신문이 비치되는 자리가 따로 있어요.
examples.en: The library has a separate spot where newspapers are kept.

examples.ko: 구급상자가 학교에 비치되면 사고에 빨리 대처할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If first-aid kits are kept at school, accidents can be handled quickly.

examples.ko: 이 책은 도서관에 비치되기 전에 검사를 받아요.
examples.en: This book is inspected before it is put on the library shelves.

explain: 호텔, 병원, 도서관 같은 곳에서 필요한 물건을 미리 갖춰 둘 때 써요. 안내문에는 '비치되어 있습니다'라고 나오고, 말할 때는 '놓여 있다', '준비되어 있다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: Used for places like hotels, hospitals, and libraries that keep needed items ready in advance. Notices say '비치되어 있습니다', while in speech '놓여 있다' or '준비되어 있다' is easier.

examples.en: A new air conditioner was installed in the classroom.

examples.ko: 이 건물 입구에는 카메라가 설치돼 있어요.
examples.en: Cameras are installed at the entrance of this building.
When the app is installed, an icon appears.
A traffic light will be installed in front of the crosswalk.
I want to delete the installed program.
With the elevator installed, it got more convenient.

explain: '설치하다'는 하는 사람이 중심이고, '설치되다'는 이미 달려 있는 결과 상태가 중심이에요. 기계·프로그램에 쓰고, 가구는 보통 '놓다'를 써요. 앱이나 프로그램은 '깔리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '설치하다' focuses on the person doing it, '설치되다' on the resulting state. It is used for machines and programs; for furniture, people usually say '놓다'. '깔리다' is a more casual word for apps and programs.

examples.ko: 초콜릿은 실온에 두면 녹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Chocolate can melt if left at room temperature.
Most metals are solid at room temperature.
This bread can be stored at room temperature.

examples.ko: 냉장고에서 꺼낸 우유가 실온으로 돌아올 때까지 기다려요.
examples.en: I wait until the milk from the fridge returns to room temperature.

examples.ko: 이 소스는 개봉 후에는 실온 보관이 안 돼요.
examples.en: This sauce can't be stored at room temperature once opened.

examples.ko: 실온 상태의 물을 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to drink water at room temperature.

explain: 음식이나 약의 보관 방법을 말할 때 '냉장', '냉동'과 나란히 자주 나와요. '상온'도 비슷하게 쓰지만, 포장지에는 '실온 보관'이라고 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 방 안 공기의 온도를 말하는 '실내 온도'와도 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It often sits beside '냉장' (refrigerated) and '냉동' (frozen) when talking about storing food or medicine. '상온' is used similarly, but packages often say '실온 보관'. It is also close to '실내 온도' (indoor temperature).

examples.en: Only ten percent of the battery is left.
Please check how much ink is left in the printer.
How much fuel is left now?

examples.ko: 주유소에 가기 전에 연료 잔량도 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before going to the gas station, I also checked the remaining fuel.

examples.ko: 물통에 물이 얼마 남았는지 잔량부터 확인해요.
examples.en: I first check how much water is left in the bottle.

examples.ko: 잔량 표시가 잘 안 보여서 불편해요.
examples.en: The remaining-amount display is hard to see, which is inconvenient.

explain: 배터리, 데이터, 연료, 잉크처럼 숫자나 눈금으로 보이는 남은 양에 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '남은 양', '얼마 남았어요?'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for remaining amounts shown by numbers or gauges, such as battery, data, fuel and ink. In daily talk people also just say '남은 양' or '얼마 남았어요?'.

examples.en: I loaded the truck full of cargo.

examples.ko: 이 차는 최대 이 톤까지 적재할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This vehicle can carry up to two tons.
The work of loading containers onto the ship is in full swing.
It's dangerous to load too much cargo.

examples.ko: 적재한 물건이 떨어지지 않게 끈으로 묶었어요.
examples.en: I tied the loaded goods with a rope so they wouldn't fall.
Boxes are piled up in the warehouse, so there's not enough space.

explain: 트럭, 배, 창고에 짐을 싣거나 쌓아 둘 때 써요. 일상에서는 '싣다'(실어요)를 쓰고, 적재는 물류나 안내문에서 '적재 중량'처럼 많이 나와요. 반대로 짐을 내리는 것은 '하역하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for loading or stacking cargo onto trucks, ships or into warehouses. In daily talk people use '싣다' (실어요), while 적재 appears in logistics and notices, as in '적재 중량'. Unloading is '하역하다'.

examples.en: The mechanic is servicing the plane.
I went to the garage to get my car serviced.
The city redid the old road.
We need to put the rules in order again.
I'll use the equipment again after servicing it.
We service the machines every month.

explain: '고치다'는 고장 난 것을 수리하는 거고, 정비하다는 문제가 생기기 전에 점검하고 손봐서 잘 쓸 수 있게 만드는 거예요. 차, 비행기뿐 아니라 길, 규칙, 제도에도 써요. 자동차 가게 이름에 '정비'가 많이 보여요.
explain_en: '고치다' is fixing something broken, while 정비하다 is checking and adjusting things before problems arise so they work well. It applies to cars and planes but also to roads, rules, and systems. You often see '정비' in auto shop names.

examples.ko: 공원 입구에 '잔디 출입 금지' 팻말이 있어요.
examples.en: At the park entrance there's a 'Keep off the grass' sign.
The field's owner put up a sign by the road.

examples.ko: 응원하는 사람들이 손에 팻말을 들고 있어요.
examples.en: The supporters are holding placards in their hands.

examples.ko: 팻말에 쓰인 글씨가 너무 작아서 안 보여요.
examples.en: The writing on the sign is too small to see.
The sign had fallen over in the wind.

examples.ko: 공항에서 이름이 적힌 팻말을 든 사람을 찾았어요.
examples.en: At the airport, I found the person holding a sign with my name.

explain: '팻말을 세우다', '팻말을 들다', '팻말을 붙이다'처럼 써요. 길에 세우는 안내판은 '표지판', 가게 위에 단 건 '간판'이라서 쓰임이 달라요. 시위나 응원, 공항 마중에서 손에 드는 판에도 팻말을 써요.
explain_en: Use it with 세우다 (set up), 들다 (hold), 붙이다 (attach). Road signs are 표지판 and shop signs are 간판, so those are different. It also covers the boards held up at protests, cheering events, and airport pickups.

examples.ko: 비행기를 타기 전에 휴대품 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: Before boarding the plane, I went through a carry-on belongings check.

examples.ko: 내릴 때 휴대품을 두고 내리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to leave your belongings behind when you get off.

examples.ko: 지갑과 열쇠 같은 휴대품은 사물함에 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please put personal items like your wallet and keys in the locker.
Do you have any belongings to declare when entering the country?
I asked a staff member where the cloakroom is.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 필요한 휴대품 목록을 적어 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote a list of the items I need to carry for the trip.

explain: 몸에 지니거나 들고 다니는 물건을 말해요. '소지품'과 비슷한데, '휴대품'은 공항, 세관, 안내문처럼 격식 있는 곳에서 더 자주 보여요. 비행기에 부치는 큰 짐과는 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: It means items you carry on your person or in your hands. It is similar to '소지품', but '휴대품' shows up more in formal places like airports, customs and notices. It is distinguished from large bags that you check in on a flight.
